title: perf: check large rational frames with the smaller dual Gram matrix
body:
`nondegenerate(U)` builds a Gram matrix with one row per basis vector, even when the frame fills almost the entire ambient space. This change checks large frames using their smaller Euclidean annihilator. A codimension-one frame needs a 1×1 matrix instead of an `(h-1)×(h-1)` matrix. All arithmetic remains exact and integral.

The two existing factored mixed-point cut customers (ambient dimensions 10 and 12) produce identical complete audit payloads and selected-frame hashes. Three fresh processes per variant give median complete batch wall time **3.380353 → 3.130144 seconds**, a **7.4% time reduction**. Median peak RSS is 92,288 → 92,744 KiB. This measures those two customers, including process startup, construction, scalar verification, rational cuts and compiled nesting. It does not establish a multiplication speedup or change κ.

### Exact criterion

The implementation extracts and reuses the integer kernel construction already in `orthogonal`. For `G=9I-J`, `h!=9`, and a full-row-rank Euclidean annihilator `A` of `U`, nondegeneracy of `G|U` is equivalent to invertibility of `A G^-1 A^T`. Since `G^-1=(I+J/(9-h))/9`, the checked integral matrix is

```text
(9-h) A A^T + (A1)(A1)^T.
```

The original direct check remains for small frames and ambient dimension nine. Dependent input rows still fail. Extracting the kernel helper preserves orthogonal-complement outputs.

### Validation and measurements

- **32 tests pass** across `test_rational_span_frames.py`, `test_mixed_point.py`, `test_block_carry.py`, `test_joint_return.py` and `test_early_sharing_and_centers.py`.
- The four new tests include **2,432 independent dense Fraction-oracle comparisons**, dimension-nine degeneracy, a valid negative Gram gap, dependent presentations and orthogonal-complement properties.
- All six complete baseline/patched benchmark payloads agree exactly; both customers certify their cuts and compiled forward/reverse nesting. A fresh patched-checkout rerun reproduces combined result SHA256 `faa0f9c0159a6e70d4e2cfcdb4012ea62ef350bd26b81312d11da4a770f8b218`.
- `git diff --check` passes. Base: `3b6b66891c0ac888521cf591fe306c6286601d4f`.
- CPython 3.12.3, Linux aarch64, CPU affinity and quota of one CPU, nice 15, 4 GiB memory limit. Filesystem caches were not flushed. Each sample is a fresh process; execution order was baseline 1, patched 1, patched 2, baseline 2, baseline 3, patched 3.

| Sample | Baseline wall (s) | Patched wall (s) | Baseline peak RSS (KiB) | Patched peak RSS (KiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 3.380353288 | 3.130143942 | 92384 | 92744 |
| 2 | 3.381442631 | 3.130612891 | 92224 | 92744 |
| 3 | 3.330750942 | 2.878172477 | 92288 | 92744 |

Reproduce from the checkout:

```sh
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_rational_span_frames.py
python3 -B tests/benchmark_rational_span_frames.py . batch.json --cpu 0
```

For a baseline timing comparison, use the same benchmark script against an unchanged base checkout. Run every sample in a fresh process under matching resource limits and use a fresh output path.

### Attestation

- [x] Scope: three Python files, no dependencies or certificate/manuscript changes.
- [x] Local gates: the 32 focused tests, complete benchmark rerun and whitespace check pass.
- [ ] Full repository gates: `make verify` and `make entrance-bank-verify` were not rerun locally; the broader CI results remain to be checked.
- [x] One focused performance change; all-size transfer and construction certificates retain their existing obligations.

Developed with OpenAI Codex assistance.
